title: Cross-validation and the leave-one-out shortcut
brief: Cut the data into folds and choose a ridge penalty with k-fold cross-validation, then build the hat matrix and get the leave-one-out error from a single fit.
hints: k_fold_indices needs three calls: rng.permutation(n), np.array_split(order, k), and np.sort on each piece.
In cross_val_score, create rng = np.random.default_rng(0) inside the function, so every penalty is scored on the same folds. np.setdiff1d(np.arange(n), test) gives the training rows.
best_lambda_by_cv calls cross_val_score once per penalty, takes .mean() of the k fold scores, and returns lambdas[np.argmin(cv_means)] together with the array of means.
hat_matrix: X @ np.linalg.inv(X.T @ X + lam * np.eye(d)) @ X.T. Keep the lam * np.eye(d) term. leverages is its diagonal.
loo_linear_smoother: r = y - H @ y, then divide by 1 - leverages, square, and average.
